text:
anya: starting a thread — spinning up a preprod GKE cluster in asia-south1 for GPU inference testing. need a short checklist: CNI compatibility, GPU driver install approach, nodepool sizing, quota tickets, and a handoff checklist.

devon: quick Q — are we doing VPC-native (alias IP) on this one? that changes CNI choices.

anya: yes VPC-native. we want private nodes, NAT egress, and internal LB.

marco: note: GKE + VPC-native means we should avoid CNIs that insist on custom routing. Calico is fine if run policy-only. Antrea is also ok. avoid any CNI that messes with subnet allocation.

lin: for GPUs: we install drivers via DaemonSet (nvidia-driver-installer) on our Ubuntu node images. GKE has COS image with GPU drivers baked in but we prefer Ubuntu for CI tooling.

marco: also FYI for EKS (if we replicate): amazon-vpc-cni is required by default for pod IPs on EC2. AMI must include CUDA/kernel compatibility or use bootstrap userdata to install drivers. AKS needs the NVIDIA device plugin as a daemonset too.

devon: noted. quota reminder: request GPU quota increase in GCP console for asia-south1 (T4 x10) — lead time ~48h. also request regional static IPs for internal LB.

anya: cost quick calc: 2 x n1-standard-16 + 4 x T4 per nodepool ~ estimate $2.8k/month for preprod if left on 24/7. will add a billing tag 'env:preprod-gpu'.

marco: small gotchas to watch during bootstrap:
- make sure node auto-upgrade is OFF for GPU nodepools until we've validated drivers.
- set surge/upgrade knobs low.

lin: ops snippets: taint + nodeSelector pattern we use:
```yaml
# taint nodes so only GPU workloads land here
kubectl taint nodes <node-name> nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule

# pod spec snippet
nodeSelector:
  cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool: gpu-pool
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```

devon: and driver install quick command (DaemonSet apply):
```bash
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/container-engine-accelerators/stable/nvidia-driver-installer.yaml
```

marco: validation checklist before handoff:
- all GPU nodes Ready and `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows gpu label
- `kubectl describe node` shows Allocatable GPUs
- DaemonSet for driver + device-plugin in Ready state (`kubectl get ds -n kube-system`)
- run a debug pod with `--gpus=1` and exec `nvidia-smi` to confirm drivers
- smoke test model container (small BPE/embedding run) to check OOMs/latency

cluster-bot: cluster-create: cluster "redwood-preprod-gke-asia-south1" created (proj: redwood-infra) — control plane healthy, 3 nodepools registering.

anya: perfect. one networking gotcha: since it's private cluster + Cloud NAT, make sure metadata server access is allowed and the NAT has the right source ranges for the node subnet. otherwise driver downloads fail during bootstrap.

devon: also watch LB subnet sizing — internal LB needs an IP in a subnet with enough addresses. set annotations for NEG if using serverless LB later.

lin: handoff doc items (to include in runbook): cluster name, project id, region, nodepool names and counts, GPU type/count, quota ticket IDs, cost tag, kubeconfig access path, monitoring dashboards links, oncall pager, and rollback steps (scale nodepool to 0 and fallback to CPU pool).

anya: assigning handoff to @marco for review. will add the quota ticket ID once submitted. :thumbsup:

marco: got it — I'll draft the runbook and ping SRE for an oncall dry-run.

devon: +1. once drivers validated we can enable node auto-upgrade with a small batch window.

lin: final quick command to check GPUs from inside k8s:
```bash
kubectl run -it --rm --restart=Never gpu-check --image=nvidia/cuda:11.7-base-ubuntu20.04 --limits='nvidia.com/gpu=1' -- /bin/bash -lc "nvidia-smi"
```

anya: thanks all — logging this thread into the cluster runbooks folder and will link in the handoff doc.

marco: thanks — ping when quota is in.
